transcript: Well, I made it home a whole 48 hours after returning from the Great Theater Adventure before I finally booked tickets to go see another show. So let's go to the theater. I just found out that there is a production of Hedwig and the Angry Inch that is happening in Denver that closes literally next week, and I just now found out about it, and I've always wanted to go see this show, so naturally I immediately bought tickets. Let's go! Yes! Oh, alright. See you in 90 minutes to two hours when I get to Denver. Made it to Denver in one piece, found some street parking and headed to the art, which is a former brewery turned event venue that's essentially a warehouse. And it is currently the home of the immersive Hedwig Denver, which sadly closes this weekend. The entire venue is set up with these cabaret tables and normal seating, and there's an entire pre show before the show even starts. And every performance there's essentially a new pre show. So they've had burlesque performers, singers, dancers, drag performers, there was a raffle and a costume contest. Just a ton of fun before the show even starts. And then the production of Hedwig was freaking incredible. Obviously, I had to stop taking footage at this point, so keep watching footage of the pre show while I talk about the actual show. But the lighting design in this production, especially during origin of love, was just Incredible. Absolutely took my breath away. And Clark Dustin Jones, who played Hedwig, was just so good. His crowd work, his vocals just in. An incredible overall performer. And it was so great to finally get to see a full production of Hedwig after being in love with this cast recording since the 90s when I was way too young to be listening to this cast recording. But this show is so fun and so immersive and absolutely must be seen in it, especially in a very intimate venue like this one. And while this production is sadly closing tonight, and I believe the final performance is completely sold out, you can definitely still follow their socials. Especially if this show ever comes back, I would love to see them do this again. It can be so hard to find shows like this, especially that are doing such an incredibly limited run, but following their socials is such a great way to find out about future productions.
